title: Grade-10 Prerequisites — Physics readiness check (foundations for IGCSE 0625)
note: This tests the PREREQUISITES for grade 10 — what he should already know before starting IGCSE Physics 0625. It deliberately does NOT test grade-10 content itself (that is next year's material). Sections mirror the IGCSE topics so you can see which foundation feeds which upcoming topic.

topics.name: Maths & practical skills (underpin all of physics)

questions.text: Rearrange a simple formula: from speed = distance / time, make distance the subject.
Substitute numbers into a formula and give the answer with the correct unit.
Read a measurement accurately from a ruler, a measuring cylinder and a thermometer.
Read a simple line graph: what does a steeper line (the gradient) tell you?
Write a large and a small number in powers of ten (e.g. 3000 and 0.005).
Calculate the area of a rectangle and the volume of a box.
Use a fraction, a decimal and a percentage in a simple calculation.
State the units used for length, mass and time.
Calculate speed from distance and time.
Read a distance–time graph: what do a steep line and a flat line mean?
Explain the difference between mass and weight.
Use the idea of density to explain why some things float and others sink.
Describe what balanced and unbalanced forces do to motion.
Give an example of friction and of gravity acting as forces.
Find the turning effect of a force (moment = force × distance).
Name some energy stores and describe one energy transfer.
State that energy is conserved — it is not created or destroyed.
Explain in everyday words what 'work' and 'power' mean.
Use pressure = force / area; why does a sharp knife cut more easily than a blunt one?
Describe how the particles are arranged and move in solids, liquids and gases.
Name the changes of state: melting, boiling, evaporation, condensation, freezing.
Explain the difference between heat (thermal energy) and temperature.
Describe conduction, convection and radiation, with an example of each.
Explain why evaporation causes cooling.
Describe what happens to most materials when they are heated (expansion).
Explain how sound travels, and why it cannot travel through a vacuum.
Explain what causes an echo.
Say which feature of a sound makes it louder, and which makes it higher in pitch.
State the law of reflection and describe what a plane mirror does to light.
Describe how light bends (refracts) when it passes from air into glass or water.
Describe what a prism does to white light.
Explain why a red object looks red.
Describe electric current as a flow of electrons; give an example of a conductor and an insulator.
Show where an ammeter goes to measure the current in a series circuit.
Say what happens to the current when you add more lamps in a series circuit.
Draw the standard symbols for a cell, switch, lamp, ammeter and voltmeter.
Describe the difference between a series and a parallel circuit.
Explain what voltage is and how a voltmeter is connected to a component.
Use the basic idea that resistance = voltage / current.
Describe a magnet's field, and how to make an electromagnet stronger.
Describe the basic structure of an atom: a nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it.
Name what is in the Solar System (Sun, planets, moons) in simple terms.
Explain day and night, and the seasons, using the Earth's spin and orbit.
State that gravity is what keeps planets and moons in their orbits.
